ideas.title: Self-Sensing Magnetron: The Food's RF Load Tells You When It's Done

new_nodes.label: Reflected-power load-impedance sensing
new_nodes.detail: Food's changing water content shifts the cavity's RF load; the reflected-power curve settles as the food reaches its target state.

new_nodes.label: Directional coupler and reflected-power detector
new_nodes.detail: A small RF tap on the waveguide replaces guesswork with a measurement, adding no heater, lamp, or extra sensor body.

new_nodes.label: Infers food doneness from RF load change
new_nodes.detail: Ends the cycle when the food's electrical state indicates it is ready, instead of when a timer runs out.

new_edges.to: Infers food doneness from RF load change

new_edges.from: Infers food doneness from RF load change

ideas.rationale: The appliance senses doneness directly from the food, so the user gets a 'ready' signal that reflects the actual state of the food rather than an elapsed-time guess.

ideas.title: Sniffing Vent: The Kitchen Smells Done and Tells the User

new_nodes.label: Metal-oxide volatile organic compound (VOC) sensing
new_nodes.detail: A heated tin-oxide sensor changes resistance as food aromas such as toast, popcorn, or roasting meat peak and then fall.

new_nodes.label: Vent-mounted MOX gas sensor
new_nodes.detail: A tiny sensor placed in the louvre airflow, cheaper than the bell striker assembly it replaces.

new_nodes.label: Detects aroma peak as doneness signal
new_nodes.detail: Triggers the end-of-cycle alert when the food's smell reaches its cooked peak.

new_edges.to: Detects aroma peak as doneness signal

new_edges.from: Detects aroma peak as doneness signal

ideas.rationale: Smell is one of the oldest human cues for 'ready', so the appliance replies to the food's own signal instead of a mechanical ding that carries no information about the food.

ideas.title: Tactile Timer Knob: The Dial Taps You on the Wrist When Done

new_nodes.label: Cam-driven haptic pulse
new_nodes.detail: The existing timer cam shaft is profiled so the knob ratchets and buzzes in a rhythm at zero, with no speaker or extra electronics.

new_nodes.label: Pulsing tactile timer knob
new_nodes.detail: The knob returns to zero and vibrates in a pattern readable by touch, from the same spring-return mechanism already present.

new_nodes.label: Signals doneness through touch
new_nodes.detail: Gives feedback to users who cannot see the display or hear the bell, and to anyone in a noisy kitchen.

ideas.rationale: Replacing the audible bell with a felt pulse from the knob itself gives a ready signal that works without sight or hearing and costs nothing extra in parts.

ideas.title: The Food Wears Its Own Ready Dot

new_nodes.label: Irreversible thermochromic time-temperature indicator
new_nodes.detail: A food-safe ink dot turns from clear to red once it has held about 75 °C, and it stays red.

new_nodes.label: Food-safe thermochromic readiness dot
new_nodes.detail: Printed on the plate, cup, or wrapper so the food carries its own indicator, with no window or lamp in the appliance.

new_nodes.label: Shows readiness by colour change on the food vessel
new_nodes.detail: Lets the user check the food from across the room or through a closed door.

new_edges.to: Shows readiness by colour change on the food vessel

new_edges.from: Shows readiness by colour change on the food vessel

ideas.rationale: Moving the readiness signal from the appliance onto the food itself removes the lamp entirely and gives a direct, unambiguous answer to whether this particular dish is hot all the way through.

ideas.title: Heat-Map Window: A Thermal Eye Replaces the Lamp

new_nodes.label: Infrared thermopile imaging through germanium window
new_nodes.detail: A germanium window passes long-wave infrared while blocking visible light; a sub-wavelength mesh keeps microwaves out, so the sensor sees surface heat.

new_nodes.label: Low-resolution thermopile sensor array (8x8)
new_nodes.detail: A cheap IR array behind the window paints a colour heat map of the food's surface temperature.

new_nodes.label: Displays hot and cold spots and surface temperature
new_nodes.detail: Shows when the whole dish is hot, not just the centre, and exposes standing-wave cold spots as they form.

new_edges.from: Infrared thermopile imaging through germanium window
Infrared thermopile imaging through germanium window

new_edges.to: Infrared thermopile imaging through germanium window
Displays hot and cold spots and surface temperature

new_edges.from: Displays hot and cold spots and surface temperature

ideas.rationale: A thermal view shows the user the actual temperature distribution of the food, so they can judge doneness from what they see rather than from a lamp that only shows the food's colour.

ideas.title: Wrist-Buzz Bell

new_nodes.label: Wearable haptic band
new_nodes.detail: A watch or ring that vibrates on your wrist when the oven finishes, replacing the striker and bell entirely.

new_nodes.label: Bluetooth Low Energy pairing
new_nodes.detail: The oven sends a short BLE packet that the paired wearable converts into a buzz.

new_nodes.label: Wireless communications
new_nodes.detail: Short-range radio signalling between appliance and personal device.

ideas.rationale: The end-of-cook signal reaches you on your body wherever you are in the office, so you never have to stand by the oven to hear the bell.

ideas.title: Fan-Pulse Alarm

new_nodes.label: Cooling fan airflow pattern
new_nodes.detail: The existing exhaust fan pulses through a recognisable speed-and-whirr rhythm to signal completion, so no extra parts are needed.

new_nodes.label: Fan speed PWM control
new_nodes.detail: Pulse-width modulation of the fan motor that already exists in the cavity cooling circuit.

ideas.rationale: Reusing the cooling fan as the alarm removes the bell's cost entirely and produces a distinctive pattern audible across a shared kitchen, so the user can wander off and still know when to return.

new_nodes.detail: A printed code on the food pack encodes the cook duration to the second, so no dial or cam is needed.

new_nodes.label: Optical code reading

new_nodes.label: Computer vision
new_nodes.detail: Image capture and decoding of printed machine-readable patterns.

new_nodes.label: Remote time entry from anywhere
new_nodes.detail: Cooking time is set by scanning the pack at your desk, not by turning a knob at the oven.

ideas.title: Joule Clock

new_nodes.label: Energy-metered cooking via current sensing
new_nodes.detail: The controller integrates delivered energy (watt-seconds) from mains current sensing and stops at a target dose.

new_nodes.label: Energy-count controller
new_nodes.detail: Firmware on the existing control board replaces the synchronous motor cam timer.

new_nodes.label: Power electronics
new_nodes.detail: Measurement and control of electrical power flow in the magnetron supply.

new_nodes.label: Cooks to delivered energy target
new_nodes.detail: Cooking ends after a set amount of energy, which is set remotely in an app.

ideas.rationale: Stopping on delivered energy instead of elapsed time lets you set and forget the job from your desk, and the cam and motor timer are no longer needed.

ideas.title: Team-Channel Chime

new_nodes.label: Cloud alert to team channel
new_nodes.detail: The oven posts a completion message to the shared kitchen's messaging channel, so the bell is replaced by a notification to everyone.

new_nodes.label: Workplace messaging API
new_nodes.detail: A webhook from the oven's Wi-Fi module into the office's existing chat tool.

new_nodes.label: Network systems
new_nodes.detail: Internet-connected appliance messaging and cloud event routing.

ideas.rationale: The office worker is told the food is ready on their phone or in the team chat wherever they are, so the bell no longer has to be heard from beside the oven.

new_nodes.label: Primary-current load sensor (shunt on HV transformer primary)
new_nodes.detail: A small current shunt and comparator on the transformer primary reads how much power the magnetron is pulling, which falls as water content drops.

new_nodes.label: Load-impedance change detection via primary current
new_nodes.detail: The magnetron's changing load shifts primary-side current, and a comparator flags the knee of the curve as the food finishes.

new_nodes.label: Infers doneness from RF load absorption
new_nodes.detail: Senses the food's own state instead of counting seconds, so the appliance closes the loop on the cooking itself.
